notes: Specialist importer profile of the historical Michel domaine: four centuries of Cornas growing, Joseph Michel's 1956 domaine bottling, Robert Michel taking over in 1975, the growth from 1.5 to eight hectares, the Chaillot/Reynard/Tézier and La Geynale sites, the 1910 Geynale planting, retirement after the 2006 vintage and selective destemming.
title: Robert Michel — Cornas

notes: Specialist importer article on Noël Verset: the Chaillots, Sabarotte and Champelrose sites, divestment of vines from the late 1980s, the 2001 sale of his largest parcel, winemaking under his own name until 2006, the Reynard sale to Thierry Allemand, the Sabarotte sale to Clape and Courbis, and the 1912-planted half hectare in Chaillots passing to his nephew Franck Balthazar.
title: The genius of Verset Cornas

notes: Specialist importer profile documenting that Thierry Allemand worked by day for Joseph Michel and then Robert Michel while helping Noël Verset at night, that Verset sold him early-twentieth-century Reynard vines, that he is 'a disciple of no one's', his minimal-sulfur and no-racking regime, and the five Sans Soufre vintages seen by the importer.
title: Allemand — Cornas

notes: Specialist importer profile stating that Auguste Clape was the village's first producer to bottle his own wine in 1957, describing Pierre-Marie Clape working alongside his father from 1989 and grandson Olivier, the acquisition of century-old vines from Noël Verset, the concrete/old-wood cellar and the blend across five to six cuvées.
title: Clape — Cornas

notes: Specialist importer profile recording that Franck Balthazar left a textile factory job in 2002, acquired a 1914 planting of Petite Syrah in Chaillot from Noël Verset alongside older family vines in Mazards and La Côte, ploughs with a horse, and ferments whole-cluster with native yeasts in concrete before old demi-muids.
title: Franck Balthazar

notes: Importer profile identifying Robert Michel as Vincent Paris's uncle, recording a 1997 first vintage, the first two wines made with his uncle, vines inherited from his grandfather, and vines rented and then purchased from his uncle including Geynale in the Cornas amphitheatre.
title: Vincent Paris

notes: Specialist importer profile recording Chave Hermitage production from 1481, the current father-and-son generation of Gérard and Jean-Louis Chave, the multi-site composition of the flagship Hermitage with Bessards as its essential climat, and a traditionally styled Saint-Joseph rouge from the historic centre of that appellation.
title: Jean-Louis Chave

notes: Specialist importer profile recording that the Jamet brothers took charge of the family domaine on Joseph Jamet's retirement in the mid-1980s, that they farm 25 plots across 17 lieux-dits, that not every site enters the flagship wine each year, and describing mostly whole-cluster fermentation and 20% new wood.
title: Jamet — Côte Rôtie

notes: Specialist importer profile placing Gonon among the old-school Saint-Joseph growers based in the original appellation around Tournon, Mauves and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, recording the purchase of Raymond Trollat's 1915 planting on his retirement, the Coteau des Oliviers Marsanne planted in 1958 and Roussanne in 1974, horse ploughing, sélection massale and whole-cluster fermentation in open wooden vats.
title: Pierre Gonon

notes: First-party estate chronology: Francis Vernay creating the estate and planting the first vines at Coteau de Vernon, the 1940 first Coteau de Vernon cuvée, Georges Vernay taking over from his father in 1953 and the estate's own 'saved' language, Les Chaillées de l'Enfer in 1992, and Christine Vernay taking over in 1996 with Terrasses de l'Empire, Maison Rouge and La Blonde du Seigneur.
title: The Estate's History — Domaine Vernay

notes: Official growers' organisation profile describing Georges Vernay as a man of vision who worked to rebuild the hillsides and rescue Viognier from obscurity, nicknamed the 'Pope of Condrieu'; Christine Vernay succeeding him in 1996, finishing the Coteau de Vernon reconstruction and converting the domaine to organic growing; the estate's Côte-Rôtie, Condrieu and Saint-Joseph range; and Francis Vernay's 1930s hectare of Viognier on Coteau de Vernon.
publisher: Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu
title: Domaine Georges Vernay — Condrieu

notes: Official growers' organisation profile recording that André Perret returned to his local area to plant vines and develop the Condrieu AOC in the 1980s, a first estate vintage in 1983, 13 hectares of which 5.5 in Condrieu, and the Coteau de Chéry and Clos Chanson bottlings.
publisher: Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu
title: André Perret — Condrieu

notes: Official growers' organisation profile recording that Yves Cuilleron took over the family domaine in 1987 when it held 3.5 hectares in Condrieu and Saint-Joseph, and that it now covers 90 hectares across six Northern Rhône AOCs plus IGP and Vin de France.
publisher: Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu
title: Cave Yves Cuilleron — Condrieu

notes: Official growers' organisation profile recording that Yves Cuilleron, Pierre Gaillard and François Villard began the Seyssuel project in 1996 with a first vintage in 1998, that the project farms 12 hectares on the Seyssuel hillsides planted to Syrah and Viognier, and that Sotanum, Héluicum and Taburnum are IGP Collines Rhodaniennes wines.
publisher: Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu
title: Les Vins de Vienne — Condrieu

notes: Long-form first-person interview with René-Jean Dard: a 1983 first vintage together but beginning 'properly' in 1984, land accumulated by renting from owners across Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage and Saint-Joseph, ploughing instead of herbicides from the mid-1980s, an explicit refusal of organic certification as a logo, 10–15 day whole-bunch red maceration with destemming when sunburn requires sorting, fermentation in large wood, one daily cap break, 500-litre demi-muid ageing, and sulfur used when a wine needs it.
title: Dard et Ribo — winemaker interview

notes: Importer interview in which René-Jean Dard states that making natural wine should not be a goal in itself but a tool for better wine, and describes making sulfur-free wines from the age of fifteen following his father's practice.
title: An Interview with René-Jean Dard of Dard and Ribo

notes: First-party wine page recording that the Ongrie cuvée was created in 1984 from 100% Marsanne vinified exclusively in 228- and 400-litre oak, at a time when most Saint-Péray production came from the traditional method and still wines were vinified in tank, and describing Alain Voge as the precursor of barrel work in Saint-Péray.
title: AOC Saint-Péray — Ongrie

notes: First-party wine page recording a 100% Marsanne traditional-method brut nature with a second fermentation in bottle and four years on lattes, and stating that the domaine perpetuates the Saint-Péray traditional-method tradition that made the region's reputation from the 1830s.
title: AOC Saint-Péray — Les Bulles d'Alain

notes: Importer profile recording that Hervé Souhaut created Domaine Romaneaux-Destezet with Béatrice Souhaut in 1993 at Arlebosc in the Ardèche hills above Saint-Joseph, that the range includes Saint-Joseph Syrah alongside Vallée du Doux wines, and describing whole-bunch spontaneous fermentation, gentle hand punch-downs and sulfur limited to 25 mg/L.
title: Domaine Romaneaux-Destezet (Hervé Souhaut)

notes: Importer profile recording that Alain Graillot returned home to Crozes-Hermitage to start his own domaine in 1985, that his sons Maxime and Antoine have been in charge since 2008, and describing hand harvesting, organic farming, whole-cluster fermentation and ageing in one- to three-year-old Burgundy barrels.
title: Alain Graillot

notes: Importer profile recording a sixth-generation family estate in Gervans, Laurent Fayolle taking control in 2002 when his father and uncle divided the family domaine, and seven hectares of parcels in the granite hills behind the hill of Hermitage across Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage and Saint-Péray.
title: Laurent Fayolle

notes: Reference-guide producer entry recording that the Gripa family arrived in Saint-Péray in the seventeenth century and settled at Mauves around 1850, that Fabrice Gripa has run the domaine since 2001 after his father Bernard, and that its 18 hectares span Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray including Les Figuiers, Les Pins and Le Berceau.
title: Domaine Bernard Gripa

notes: First-party estate site recording that Stéphane Robert created Domaine du Tunnel in 1994 with 2.5 hectares, that the estate works Cornas, Saint-Péray and Saint-Joseph and added Condrieu in 2013, that it now farms about 12 hectares, and that its name comes from a rehabilitated early-twentieth-century railway tunnel at the lieu-dit Barras in Saint-Péray.
title: Domaine du Tunnel — Stéphane Robert

notes: Trade editorial recording that Jean-Michel Stéphan established his domaine at Tupin-Semons in Côte-Rôtie in 1991 after working at Jean-Paul Brun's Domaine des Terres Dorées in Beaujolais, that he has added no sulfites since 1997, and describing indigenous-yeast carbonic work, old barrels, no fining or filtration, plots at Bassenon, Coteaux de Tupin, Les Bercheries and Verenay, and massale Sérine replanting.
title: Jean-Michel Stephan: outstanding, natural Côte-Rôtie

notes: First-party house chronology: founded by Etienne Guigal at Ampuis in 1946, Marcel Guigal taking over management in 1961, Philippe Guigal joining as winemaker in 1997, the Vidal-Fleury, Château d'Ampuis, Jean-Louis Grippat, de Vallouit, Domaine de Bonserine, Château de Nalys and Château d'Aqueria acquisitions, and the house cooperage from 2003.
title: History of Maison Guigal since 1946

notes: First-party house chronology recording the 1808 creation of Calvet et Compagnie in the rue de l'Hermitage at Tain, Michel Chapoutier's first plot selections (Sélections Parcellaires) in 1989, and his assumption of control in 1990 with the beginning of biodynamic cultivation.
title: History of the winery M. Chapoutier

notes: First-party house chronology recording the 1834 founding by Antoine Jaboulet on the hill of l'Hermitage at Tain-l'Hermitage, the creation of Hermitage La Chapelle in 1961, Gérard Jaboulet taking up the torch from 1977 until his death in 1997, and Caroline Frey assuming control in 2006 and beginning the conversion to organic and biodynamic farming.
title: Our History — Domaines Paul Jaboulet Aîné

notes: First-party owner site recording that Château Grillet was acquired by the Pinault family in 2011, that the vineyard lies at Vérin near the Condrieu and Côte-Rôtie appellations, and that it received its own AOC in 1936 as one of the very few French monopole appellations.
title: Artémis Domaines — estates
